## Why

S631's round-1 full suite failed once with `TestWaveHeldMemberStartsAfterTheEarlierLands ... item failed: run ork-20261127-205645-9e55: mkdir .../runs/ork-20261127-205645-9e55: file exists`. The test passes on main and in the worktree, so this was an ID collision, not a logic failure. A run ID is `"ork-"` plus the time to the second plus `Deps.randHex()` (`internal/engine/engine.go:117-124`, `:428`), and `randHex` is 2 random bytes (4 hex digits). Two runs created in the same second collide with probability about 1/65536 per pair. `runrec.Store.Create` (`internal/runrec/store.go:103`) then fails on `os.Mkdir`, and the run fails. The red slice check stuck through rounds 2 and 3 because the product had not changed.

Owner decision (adj 657, Jon, session 8d711f67, 2026-11-27): use 4 random bytes (8 hex digits) for run, chain and wave IDs, and retry the create up to 8 times on file exists. Run IDs are the only one of the three that creates anything on disk. `newChainID` and `newWaveID` (`internal/daemon/runs.go:1375`, `:1672`) only build a label stamped on run records. So the retry applies to the run create in `engine.New`, and the widening applies to all three (see Owner needed).

Owner decisions, 2026-11-27: adj 657 (4 bytes, 8 tries) and adj 660 (chain and wave IDs are only widened; only the run ID create retries).

- `TestNewRetriesTheRunIDWhenItsDirectoryExists` (`internal/engine/engine_test.go`): the harness `RandHex` returns "aaaaaaaa" then "bbbbbbbb", and the run directory `ork-20261019-161201-aaaaaaaa` already exists in `h.store`. `New` succeeds, `Snapshot().ID` is `ork-20261019-161201-bbbbbbbb`, and `RandHex` was called twice. It fails first because `New` returns the "file exists" error from `Store.Create`.
- `TestNewGivesUpAfterEightCollidingRunIDs` (`internal/engine/engine_test.go`): `RandHex` always returns "aaaaaaaa" and that directory exists. `New` returns an error where `errors.Is(err, os.ErrExist)` holds, `RandHex` was called exactly 8 times, and no other run directory exists. ## Implement

1. In `internal/engine/engine.go`, change `randHex` to `make([]byte, 4)`, so the default suffix is 8 hex digits. Change the `Deps.RandHex` comment at line 61 to "eight hex digits for run ids; nil is random".
2. In `New` (`:428-455`), call `d.now()` once and format the time stamp once, before the create. Add a constant for the attempt count (`runIDTries = 8`). Loop up to `runIDTries` times: build `id := "ork-" + stamp + "-" + d.randHex()` and call `d.Store.Create(...)` with the same record apart from `ID`. Stop on success. When `errors.Is(err, os.ErrExist)`, try again with a new `randHex()`. Return any other error at once. After the last attempt, return the last error, which still wraps `os.ErrExist`. Add the `errors` and `os` imports if they are missing.
3. In `internal/daemon/runs.go`, change `make([]byte, 2)` to `make([]byte, 4)` in `newChainID` (`:1376`) and `newWaveID` (`:1673`). Add no retry there, because neither ID creates a file (see Owner needed).
4. Update the two `{4}` regexes to `{8}`: `internal/daemon/wave_test.go:51` and `internal/daemon/runs_test.go:2550`. Add the three new engine tests to `internal/engine/engine_test.go` and the two ID-width tests to `internal/daemon/runs_test.go`. Pre-create a run directory with `os.Mkdir(h.store.RunDir(id), 0o700)`. Do not change the harness `RandHex` returning "a1b2"; any string is accepted.
5. In `docs/design.md:3483`, change `xxxx` to `xxxxxxxx` in the wave ID form. In `docs/state.md:495-496`, lengthen the example IDs to 8 hex digits (`ork-20261018-161200-a1b2c3d4`, `wave-20261018-161150-77aa88bb`). Leave the legacy check-directory text (`docs/design.md:2498`, `docs/state.md:479`) and `legacySpecDir` (`internal/daemon/speccheck_state.go:115`) alone, because they name older directories.
6. Run `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l .`. Run `slicer check`.
